title: Unmarked algebraic relative dualizing complexes over arbitrary rings are isomorphic
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a flat finitely presented homomorphism of arbitrary commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Put $B=A\otimes_R A$, $p_1(a)=a\otimes1$, and give $A$ its $B$-module structure via multiplication. Use the module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], derived scalar extension and diagonal object [def-trf-affine-diagonal-module-data], and derived Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on the one-object ringed site. For $T\in D(A)$ put $T_1=T\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A,p_1}B$. Say $T$ is $R$-perfect if it is pseudo-coherent over $A$ [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex] and has finite Tor amplitude over $R$: there are integers $a\le b$ with $H^i(T\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q)=0$ for all $R$-modules $Q$ and $i\notin[a,b]$. If $M,N\in D(A)$ are $R$-perfect and $R\operatorname{Hom}_B(A,M_1)$ and $R\operatorname{Hom}_B(A,N_1)$ are isomorphic to $A[0]$ in $D(B)$, then $M\cong N$ in $D(A)$. The isomorphism need not preserve any chosen diagonal class. No Noetherian or nonzero-ring hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Choose a presentation $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$ using [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Let $C=C_{P\to A}(P)[n]$. By [lem-sfb-arbitrary-polynomial-dual-properties], $C$ is $R$-perfect and the scalar map $h:A[0]\to R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,C)$ is invertible. This argument also applies to the zero algebra; its derived category has only the zero object.

proof.text: For $T=M,N$ restrict its assumed diagonal isomorphism along the actual first coprojection $p_1:A\to B$. Since multiplication composed with $p_1$ is $1_A$, the restricted target is $A[0]$ with its usual $A$-action. Apply [lem-sfb-arbitrary-polynomial-diagonal-hom] to obtain an isomorphism $g_T:A[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,T)$. Only existence is required; no generator is chosen or preserved.

source.place: Tag 0E2D, lemma-uniqueness-relative-dualizing; agent polynomial-duality proof repairing the Tor hypothesis in its two evaluation applications.

proof.text: Use [lem-pod-projective-hom-evaluation-model] with a bounded-above finite-free representative of $C$, supplied by its pseudo-coherence in step 1. Let $f_T:C=C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A[0]\to T$ be the adjunct of $g_T$. Naturality of the tensor--Hom adjunction gives $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,f_T)\circ h=g_T$, since $h$ is the adjunct of $1_C$. Thus $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,f_T)$ is invertible.

source.place: Tag 0E2D, lemma-uniqueness-relative-dualizing; agent polynomial-duality proof repairing the Tor hypothesis in its two evaluation applications.

proof.text: Both $C$ and $T$ are $R$-perfect: step 1 gives this for $C$ and the hypothesis gives it for $T=M,N$. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-perfect-polynomial-dual-detection] to $f_T:C\to T$ and step 3. It follows that $f_M$ and $f_N$ are isomorphisms. The composite $f_N\circ f_M^{-1}:M\to N$ proves the assertion, with no normalization condition.
